sources.title: Does UV Radiation Cause Cancer?   | American Cancer Society
sources.reason: Confirms UV radiation is a major risk factor for skin cancers including melanoma, though doesn't isolate UVB specifically.
sources.snippet: Some things that are linked to increased UV exposure include: Spending time in the sun for recreation or work Spending a lot of time in the sun with unprotected or exposed skin Living in an area that gets a lot of sunlight Having serious sunburns (more sunburns are linked to a higher risk) Having signs of sun damage to the skin Studies have also found links between melanoma of the skin and certain sun exposure factors, including: Activities that lead to intermittent, recreational sun exposure, such as sunbathing, water sports, and taking vacations in sunny places Previous sunburns Intense sun exposure or severe sunburns as a child or adolescent Signs of sun damage to the skin Because UV rays don’t reach beyond the skin into the body, they have not been found to cause cancer in internal organs. However, some studies have shown possible links between UV rays and some other cancers, including Merkel cell carcinoma (a less common type of skin cancer) and melanoma of the eye .

sources.snippet: Both tanning beds and the sun emit harmful UVA rays — but tanning beds emit far more of them. In fact, older yet oft-cited research shows that tanning beds can emit 10 to 15 times more UVA rays than the sun.
